headline: Coastal Parking and State Park Entry Fees
reservation: Individual hotel and rental bookings are essential during the summer peak, often filling months in advance. While beach access is public, daily vehicle fees apply for Cape Henlopen and Delaware Seashore State Parks; check official state park sites for current seasonal pass or daily rate procedures.

days.title: Boardwalk Culture and Atlantic Sands

stops.name: Rehoboth Beach Boardwalk
stops.detail: Stroll the iconic wooden walkway for ocean views and local architectural character.

stops.name: Rehoboth Beach Bandstand
stops.detail: Visit the central social hub that hosts evening community events during the summer season.

days.driving: Walking destination; no vehicle travel required once parked in the town center.
days.note: Metered parking is strictly enforced in town; use the park-and-ride shuttle to avoid congestion.

days.title: Dunes and Coastal Defense

stops.name: Fort Miles Historic Site
stops.detail: Explore the World War II coastal defense installations and climb the observation tower.

stops.name: Cape Henlopen State Park
stops.detail: Bike the Gordons Pond Trail to see shifting dunes and unique salt marsh ecosystems.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; traffic between Lewes and Rehoboth varies significantly by time of day.
days.note: Bicycles are the most efficient way to travel between the state park and town trails.

days.title: Inland Bays and Quiet Reflections

stops.name: Delaware Seashore State Park
stops.detail: Visit the less developed stretches of coast south of town for beachcombing and birding.

stops.name: Rehoboth Bay Marshlands
stops.detail: Launch a kayak to observe egrets and local marine life in the sheltered bay waters.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; bridge traffic at Indian River Inlet can cause minor delays.
days.note: Check the local tide charts if planning to paddle through the shallow salt marshes.

intel.title: Summer Metering
intel.text: Downtown Rehoboth uses a tiered parking meter system from May through September. The Park and Ride lot on Route 1 is the most reliable way to avoid full garages.

intel.title: Urban Reliability
intel.text: Cellular signal is excellent throughout the town and boardwalk areas. Some remote sections of the Cape Henlopen dunes may have intermittent data coverage.

intel.title: Route 1 Corridor
intel.text: Major fuel stations and large supermarkets are concentrated along Highway 1 outside the town limits. Stock up on beach supplies before entering the residential boardwalk zone.

intel.title: Shoulder Season
intel.text: September offers warm water with fewer crowds than July. Many seasonal kiosks reduce hours after Labor Day, so check specific business listings for autumn trips.

intel.title: Pedestrian Zones
intel.text: The boardwalk is a walking-only zone during peak hours; bicycles have restricted time windows. Check the town’s official signage for current morning cycling hours.

plan.arrival: Arrive via DOV and drive 60 minutes south, utilizing the Highway 1 corridor for any needed beach supplies or groceries.
plan.vehicle: Compact cars are easiest for town parking; bicycles are highly recommended for local transit.
plan.goldenHour: Gordons Pond Trail offers unobstructed sunset views over the salt marshes and wetlands.
